h2: Neutral third-party inspection in Los Angeles: witness testing, California vessel permits and whether to outsource

Neutral third-party inspection in Los Angeles: witness testing, California vessel permits and whether to outsource

Searches for "neutral third party inspection" and "cross party witness testing" in Los Angeles usually come from a buyer and a seller who disagree, or expect to, about whether equipment meets the contract. The practical answer is an examination that both sides can watch and repeat. Atlantis performs conventional NDT, meaning UT, MT, PT and VT, on that basis. It is not an API authorized inspection agency, does not supply API inspectors and does not issue California permits.

How does cross-party witness testing work?

  1. Agree the rules before testing. Both parties sign off the procedure, the acceptance criteria with the code edition, the instruments and the calibration blocks before anyone touches the part.
  2. Notify everyone. Give each party's representative a date and enough notice to attend; a test run without the other side present invites the dispute it was meant to settle.
  3. Calibrate in front of the witnesses. UT sensitivity on the reference block, MT field checks and PT system checks are done while they watch.
  4. Record, then interpret. Readings and indications go on a shared data sheet that every party initials before anyone argues about acceptance.
  5. Separate the result from the decision. The examiner reports what was found against the agreed criteria; the contract decides what happens next.

A "neutral third party lab" is a different service: chemistry, mechanical tests or failure analysis on samples both parties send to the same laboratory.

California's pressure vessel permits

California, unlike many states, puts unfired pressure vessels under a state permit system. Cal/OSHA's Pressure Vessel Unit requires a permit to operate for air tanks over 1.5 cubic feet (with exemptions), LP-gas tanks over 125 gallons water capacity and power boilers above 15 psig, and inspections are made by the unit's inspectors or by qualified inspectors employed by insurance companies. Refinery process vessels are also tracked under the owner's API 510 program. Atlantis supports either inspector with UT thickness, weld UT, MT and PT; the inspector decides on the permit. See API 510 NDE support in California.

Third-party welding inspection

On refinery and terminal construction, welds are examined to ASME B31.3 or Section VIII as the purchase order requires, and on structural steel to AWS D1.1. A third-party welding inspector checks procedures, welder qualifications and visual quality; NDT supplies the volumetric and surface evidence. Atlantis performs VT, MT, PT and shear-wave UT of welds: ultrasonic weld inspection, magnetic particle testing in Los Angeles and penetrant testing in Los Angeles. Building permits in the city carry their own special inspection rules, so confirm with the building department who must perform those inspections.

Should you outsource NDT to a third-party provider?

  • Outsource when work comes in peaks such as turnarounds, when you need several methods for a short campaign, or when the result must be independent of the people who built or repaired the equipment.
  • Keep it in house when volume is steady, one method dominates and turnaround time on the shop floor matters more than independence.
  • Mix the two when your own technicians do routine work under your written practice and an outside ASNT Level III owns procedures, examinations and audits: see ASNT Level III consulting.

How Los Angeles providers compare

The Los Angeles market has a strong aerospace laboratory side. Mistras's Los Angeles in-lab branch in Cudahy, for example, lists Nadcap accreditation and MT, PT, UT and immersion testing for aerospace and defense parts. Field firms, including rope access specialists and tank contractors, cover refineries, terminals and the ports. Before hiring any of them, ask who the Level III behind the procedures is, whether the technicians are certified in each method under a written practice, and when the report will be issued.

Atlantis in Los Angeles

From its Houston base, Atlantis sends crews to Los Angeles, Long Beach and South Bay sites for agreed dates. Radiographic examination stays with the owner's licensed radiography contractor, as Atlantis does not perform radiography in the United States, though its Level III can review the film or digital images.
